Chapter 36

Shallow routing, and a drawer the back button closes

A shallow goto with page.state, a URL that is also a real page, and why the drawer reads history rather than a variable.

By the end of this chapter

Open a trace without losing the query that found it, and share the link anyway.

Somebody ran a query, found a slow request, and wants to see why — and then wants to look at the next one. A full navigation loses the query, the scroll position and the place in the list, and getting back means the browser’s back button *and* re-finding the row.

goto(url, { shallow: true, state }) adds a history entry — so the back button closes the drawer — without running a single load function. The results stay exactly as they were. SvelteKit 3 spells it this way instead of pushState(url, state) so that one function owns every change to the address bar, and so that the URL has to be one resolve() can vouch for.

And the URL it writes is a real page. Reloading lands on /[tenant]/traces/[traceId], which renders the same two views at full size. That combination — shallow within a session, real when shared — is what shallow routing is for, and it is why the drawer is not simply a component with an open prop.

The drawer reads history, not a variable

A local open variable that the shallow goto also happens to set is the version that looks right and is broken: the back button changes the history entry and leaves the variable true. Reading page.state directly means there is exactly one source of truth, and the browser’s own navigation is it.

Four ways to close, one implementation

Escape, the button, the backdrop and the back button all do the same thing: history.back(). Anything else leaves the history entry behind, so the back button reopens a drawer somebody just closed.

And a link that is still a link

A modifier-click or a middle-click must keep its normal meaning. Hijacking every click is how a link stops being a link — and "open in a new tab" is exactly what somebody does with a trace they want to keep while they look at the next one.

This link used to have an onclick that guarded the modifier keys by hand and then, for a plain click, pushed shallow state for the URL the address bar already showed — a no-op that *looked* like navigation, and no test said otherwise. Migrating pushState to goto(url, { shallow: true }) is what exposed it: once shallow was a word in the call, it was visibly the wrong word, because leaving the drawer for the full page is the one real navigation in the file. The fix was deletion, and e2e/trace.e2e.ts now has the test that was missing.

Every internal link is typed

resolve('/[tenant]/traces/[traceId]', { tenant, traceId }) instead of a template string. The route id is a member of a union SvelteKit generates from src/routes, so a link to a page that was renamed is a type error rather than a 404 somebody finds a week later — and eslint-plugin-svelte's no-navigation-without-resolve asks every href and every goto to go through it, for the same reason. The explore page imports it as resolvePath, because it already has a resolve of its own for time ranges, and two functions with one name are easier to read apart than to tell apart.

View transitions, in six lines and two guards

The guards matter as much as the feature. startViewTransition does not exist in every browser, and there the navigation simply happens — which is the correct fallback and needs no polyfill. And somebody who asked their system for reduced motion asked for this too; honouring it *here* rather than only in CSS means the transition is never started, which is cheaper and avoids the flash that killing a running animation produces.

There is no slide, no scale and no stagger. In a tool somebody uses for eight hours, a transition that is *noticeable* is a transition that is annoying by lunchtime.

The third guard is new with SvelteKit 3, which runs the navigation hooks for shallow navigations too. Both shallow callers in this app are the wrong shape for a cross-fade — the explore page rewrites its query string every time typing settles, and the drawer slides over a page that must stay exactly where it was — so navigation.shallow returns early before the transition is ever started.

Checkpoint

  • Opening a trace changes the URL and does not re-run any load.
  • The back button closes the drawer and the results are still there.
  • Reloading the drawer’s URL lands on a full page.
